Independent rational enumerations and factorial-moment coefficients passed 68 checks; no finite test was treated as a proof of an infinite limit.

value.rationale: A natural global hub appended to a cycle leaves typical Gaussian fluctuations unchanged but adds a strictly positive linear-order variance term; a sublinearly growing universal clique creates a standardized distribution converging to zero despite unit variance. The full k/n classification and exact finite law make this a structurally motivated counterexample to conflating Gaussian weak limits with second-moment convergence, rather than a numerical curiosity.
